and_a_sixty_four_lane_tile_is_in_the_tre: ot_a3_tile64 is LQ8S = 8 instances of ot_a3_lq8 at LANES = 8 each -- SIXTY FOUR lanes, a 128 B/cycle weight port, a shared activation port and a tile stream sequencer. Its instantiated_by is EMPTY: nothing in the design builds it, and it has never been routed. ot_a3_tensor_routed_matmul, which wraps the pipelined lane for the routed-matmul operator, is instantiated by nothing either. This is the same shape as the Sinkhorn twin that was fixed this morning -- a qualified replacement nothing instantiates -- at the largest scale in the design.
answer: THE TOKEN DATAPATH IS ONE MAC WIDE. ot_a3_engine_array's matmul route ends at ot_a3_mac_lane_pipe, which instantiates exactly ONE ot_mac_bf16_fp32_pipe; its LANES_IF of 8 is an INTERLEAVE factor -- eight output columns time-shared through that one unit to hide its five-stage latency -- not eight multipliers. The iso-area vehicle is sixteen wide. So the 2.077x peak cannot be attributed to the datapath that runs a token, and the gap is not a clock or a layout difference: it is 16x of arithmetic that is not there.
not_a_claim: ot_compute_unit's 1289.7 MHz and ot_a3_g2_cluster's 226.2 MHz are both read out of routed records; the first is closed and the second is not
this does not say ot_a3_tile64 works: it has never been routed and this repository has no bench that drives it, which is exactly why it is named here as work rather than as capability
a MAC-per-cycle count is an arithmetic width, not a throughput: what a token costs depends on operand delivery, which the three-level iso-area audit already reports as the binding constraint

producer.tool: hand-written from the instantiation graph and the routed records

question: the A100 iso-area ratio is measured on ot_compute_unit and the tokens are generated by ot_a3_engine_array, and the two share no module. HOW WIDE is each? A ratio of throughput per mm2 is a statement about MACs per cycle per unit area, so the arithmetic width of each vehicle is the thing that makes the numbers comparable or not.

vehicles_by_arithmetic_width.control_plane: the engine issue surface, not the microsequencer
vehicles_by_arithmetic_width.how: ot_a3_mac_lane_pipe -> one ot_mac_bf16_fp32_pipe, LANES_IF=8 is interleaving; the legacy ot_a3_mac_lane beside it retires one multiply-accumulate every FIVE cycles
vehicles_by_arithmetic_width.routed: NO RECORD: the umbrella route timed out twice at fifteen hours; a third is running at HEAD on materially smaller members

vehicles_by_arithmetic_width.how: ot_mac_tile at LANES = 16, plus two fakeram weight macros

vehicles_by_arithmetic_width.control_plane: the FULL microsequencer: decoder, loop stack, symbol file, view resolver, scoreboard, dependence table
vehicles_by_arithmetic_width.how: two ot_a3_lq8 instances at LANES = 8 each
eight ot_a3_lq8 at LANES = 8 under one tile stream sequencer
vehicles_by_arithmetic_width.routed: NEVER ROUTED, and instantiated by nothing

what_this_makes_the_remaining_work: the iso-area claim and the token datapath meet when the engine array's matmul route reaches a multi-lane tile instead of one interleaved unit; ot_a3_tile64 is that tile and it is already written

ot_a3_g2_cluster is the only vehicle that carries BOTH a real control plane and more than one lane, and its routed 226.2 MHz against ot_compute_unit's 1289.7 MHz at the same sixteen lanes is what the control plane costs in clock -- 5.7x, on 721,709 cells against the compute unit's own
none of this changes a token: the nine-cell matrix runs on runtime.sim, whose engines implement the same contracts at any width
